newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end with 2 pct gain on Dow, merger.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end with 2 pct gain on Dow, merger.

text.p: French shares closed on Monday with a jump of more than two percent, ending just below 2,700 on the CAC index, pushed by a storming rise on the Dow Jones stock index in New York, traders said.
Advances in the food and drinks sector, powered by news of a 20 billion stg merger between Britain's Guinness and Grand Metropolitan, also helped pump up the blue chip CAC-40 index.
The CAC-40 closed up 59.18 points or 2.25 percent at 2,693.09. The CAC-40 May futures contract was up 69 at 2,684 from Friday's close.

LVMH runs up 4.93 percent to 1,446 francs, on the back of the Guinness/Grand Met merger. The French firm which currently holds 14 percent of Guinness, will eventually get a seven percent stake in the new company GMG Brands, a source close to LVMH told Reuters.
Danone gains 2.33 percent to 880 and Pernod Ricard rises 2.87 percent to 308.50, in sympathy.

Lyonnaise des Eaux and merger partner Cie de Suez gain respectively 5.26 percent to 580 francs and 3.81 percent to 305. Traders said Exane and Kleinwort Benson were said to be heavy buyers although there had apprently been no change in recommendation.

Promodes rises 4.81 percent to 2,028 francs, after hitting historic high of 2,036 in the day. The stock is catching after last week's announcement of a link up between privately held retailer Auchan and Rinascente of Italy.
